*Fa-batna bi-janibay musarra'at... wa-bittu afuddu aghlaqa al-khitami*

[The line means, according to al-Farazdaq: the women went out from their howdahs/curtains, their virginity not having been touched by anyone before me, and they are purer than ostrich eggs, which are customarily guarded from breaking so their beauty is not lost. So they spent the night stretched out on either side of me, and I spent it opening the locks of the seals. 'Aghlaq' is the plural of 'ghalq' like 'sabab', meaning locks; and 'khitam' is what is used to seal the mouth of a bottle and the like, so its idafa is explanatory (bayaniyya), or it is an idafa of the named to the name, like 'a'wad al-siwak'. It is permissible that 'khitam' means 'makhtum', which is the vagina; and the 'aghlaq' may be meant as the sides of the hymen interlaced with the vagina, and the hymens or their sides are likened to locks by way of explicit comparison.]

When Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Malik heard that, he said: 'The hadd punishment has become obligatory upon you.' He said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, Allah has repelled the hadd from me by His saying: "And that they say what they do not do."' So he released him."

Al-Zamakhshari's commentary (al-Kashshaf) on surah 26, verse 227:

The poets are excepted: the righteous believers who remember Allah often and recite the Qur'an, and whose poetry is mostly of that kind. When they composed poetry, they composed it on the Oneness of Allah and praise of Him, on wisdom and admonition, on asceticism and good manners, on praising the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the Companions, and the righteous of the Ummah, and on meanings that are not objectionable, in which they do not become stained by sin or involved in disgrace or defect. Their satire was only as a means of defending themselves against those who satirized them. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech, except by one who has been wronged﴾ (4:148), provided it involves no transgression and no excess beyond the response to His saying: ﴿So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you﴾ (2:194).

It is related from Amr ibn Ubayd that a man from the Alawites said to him: "My chest surges with poetry." He said: "What prevents you from it, in what is not objectionable?" The principle in this matter is that poetry is a branch of speech: its goodness is like the goodness of speech, and its ugliness is like the ugliness of speech.

It has been said that those excepted are Abdullah ibn Rawahah, Hassan ibn Thabit, and the two Ka'bs: Ka'b ibn Malik and Ka'b ibn Zuhayr, and those who used to defend the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and confront the satirists of Quraysh. It is related from Ka'b ibn Malik that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Satirize them, for by Him in whose hand is my soul, it is more painful to them than arrows." [[Narrated by Abd al-Razzaq from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, from his father, who said: "When the verse ﴿As for the poets, the deviators follow them﴾ (26:224) was revealed, I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of poetry?' He said: 'The believer strives with his sword and his tongue. By Him in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, it is as if you are shooting them with arrows.'" I say: It was also narrated by this route. Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat said: Abd al-Wahhab informed us, Ibn Awf informed us, from Ibn Sirin, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Ka'b ibn Malik: "Go on," and he recited. He said: "It is more painful to them than the impact of arrows." Muslim has from Aisha, traced to the Prophet: "Satirize Quraysh, for it is more painful to them than a volley of arrows." Al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i have from the hadith of Thabit, from Anas, within a longer narration: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Leave them alone, O Umar, for it strikes them more swiftly than the spray of arrows."]] He used to say to Hassan: "Say, and the Rawh al-Qudus (Holy Spirit) is with you." [[Agreed upon, from the hadith transmitted by al-Bazzar. The wording of al-Nasa'i: He said to Hassan: "Satirize the polytheists, for the Rawh al-Qudus is with you." Al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh have, through Mujalid, from al-Sha'bi, from Jabir, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said on the day of the Confederates: "Who will protect the honour of the Muslims?" Hassan said: "I will." He said: "Then rise and satirize them, for the Rawh al-Qudus will support you."]]

He concluded the surah with a verse that speaks of nothing more awe-inspiring or terrifying, nothing more painful to the hearts of those who reflect, nor more shattering to the livers of those who ponder. This is in His saying ﴿And those who have wronged will know﴾, with its severe threat, and in His saying ﴿those who have wronged﴾ with its unrestricted generality, and in His saying ﴿what [sort of] return they will be returned to﴾ with its vagueness. Abu Bakr recited it to Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, when he appointed him as successor. [[Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim through Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mahsar, from Hisham, from his father, from Aisha, who said: "My father wrote a testament," and she mentioned it, and at its end: "And if you deviate and do wrong, then I do not know the unseen. ﴿And those who have wronged will know﴾ - the verse." Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat, in the biography of Abu Bakr, related it from al-Waqidi through multiple chains, at length.]] The righteous predecessors used to admonish one another with it and warn one another of its severity.

Explaining wrongdoing as disbelief is a rationale [[His saying "Explaining wrongdoing as disbelief is a rationale": perhaps it is from his "ta'lil" (giving a rationale), meaning he occupied himself with it, as a child is quieted with some food in place of milk, as in al-Sihah. (Editor's note: "ʿ")]], and because to fear and thus attain safety is better than to feel secure and thus attain fear.

Ibn Abbas recited: "ayya munfalat yanfalitun" (which way of escape they will escape). Its meaning: those who have wronged hope to escape the punishment of Allah, but they will come to know that there is no way for them of escape, which is salvation. O Allah, make us among those who have placed this verse before their eyes and did not neglect it, and who know that whoever does an evil deed is among those who have wronged. And Allah knows best what is correct.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the surah of the Poets, he will have the reward of ten good deeds for each of those who believed in Noah and disbelieved in him, and Hud, Shu'ayb, Salih and Ibrahim, and for each of those who disbelieved in Jesus and believed in Muhammad, peace be upon them all." [[Narrated by al-Tha'labi and Ibn Mardawayh from the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b.]]
